commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Refresh of 3505 removes the 3102/3202/3402/3403 imports and changes the direct_wage_payment_third_party_liability_applies formula, dropping the imported employer-withholding-duty conditions (logic/scope change in a merged module).
description: the generated rule treats sections 3102, 3202, 3402, and 3403 as the statutory scope of the direct-payment liability rule, not as separate runtime applicability gates

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix applies-rule required, on top of the three conditions 26 USC 3505(a) actually states, an extra conjunct that at least one imported employer-side value be true or positive (employer_required_to_collect_section_3101_tax_by_wage_deduction, employer_section_3201_tax_payment_liability > 0, amount_of_wages_for_withholding_tables > 0, employer_liability_for_chapter_withholding_tax_payment > 0), a runtime gate with no basis in the provision, whose 'For purposes of sections 3102, 3202, 3402, and 3403' opener is a scope phrase, not a condition.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/3505): 3505(a) conditions are exactly (1) a lender, surety, or other person, (2) who is not an employer under such sections with respect to the employee(s), (3) pays wages directly to the employee(s) or to an agent; nothing conditions liability on the employer's own withholding duty being live. The third disjunct in the removed gate, amount_of_wages_for_withholding_tables > 0, is a 3402(a) wage/withholding-table amount rather than any duty, which is further evidence the branch was invented rather than sourced. The commit message itself is bare ('Refresh generated section 3505 payroll rules'); the naming evidence is the PR Notes section, so this is a regeneration in which the maintainer explicitly identified and defended the semantic delta rather than a targeted bug-fix commit -- that is the main reason confidence is 0.82 rather than higher. Same commit also carries non-fidelity noise that should not be treated as the defect: whole-file YAML restyling (block scalars, list indentation), a reworded module summary, several proof-atom excerpt strings broadened to match the source text, and a commutative reorder of rules[supplied_funds_third_party_liability_limit].versions[0].formula from `rate * max(0, amount)` to `max(0, amount) * rate` (no meaning change); also an added proof atom on supplied_funds_third_party_liability. Effective dates (all 1990-01-01), entities, periods, dtypes, and the 0.25 rate are unchanged. Companion test 3505.test.yaml drops the now-unused imported employer-side inputs and renames cases; the 25 percent cap-binding case survives as supplied_funds_liability_is_capped_at_twenty_five_percent_of_amount_supplied, so cap coverage was not lost. The screening note framed this as a possible logic/scope regression; on the source text the direction is the opposite -- the pre-fix module was over-gated and the refresh re-grounds it.
triage.verifier_justification: 26 USC 3505(a), read through the pinned corpus release, conditions third-party direct-payment liability on exactly three facts (lender/surety/other person; not an employer under such sections; pays wages directly), with "For purposes of sections 3102, 3202, 3402, and 3403" serving as a scope preamble and the only employer-side reference sitting in the amount clause ("taxes ... required to be deducted and withheld from such wages by such employer"). The pre-fix formula added a fourth conjunct requiring at least one of four imported employer-side values to be true or positive, a runtime gate with no counterpart in the provision; the fix deletes it along with the four `imports:` entries, so encoded meaning changed (a direct-paying lender now correctly holds even when the employer-side imports are false/zero). Attempts to refute fail: entity, dtype, period, effective window and outputs are unchanged, so `wrong_entity_or_scope` does not fit; the disjunction was not a mis-combination of source-stated conditions, so `polarity_or_logic` does not fit; and it is not mechanical because a formula's truth conditions changed. Corroborating: the pre-fix proof atoms backing that conjunct were all `kind: import` with hashes and no `source.excerpt`, i.e. the encoding's own proof record had no source grounding for it.
triage.verifier_notes: Caveats for the reviewer: (1) the commit body is empty and the PR is framed as a regeneration ("regenerate 26 USC 3505 with axiom-encode 0.2.532 and gpt-5.5"), so this was not authored as a targeted defect repair; the fidelity reasoning appears only in the PR Notes bullet the first reader quoted. It is still a maintainer statement of why the old encoding was wrong, and the diff independently supports it. (2) The diff is a whole-file restyle (flow to block scalars, quoted excerpts), so most removed lines are cosmetic; the only meaning-bearing changes are the removed conjunct plus the four `imports:` lines. The other formula edit, supplied_funds_third_party_liability_limit, is a commutative reorder (rate * max(0, amount) -> max(0, amount) * rate) and is meaning-preserving. (3) Several proof-atom excerpt strings were lengthened or trimmed; those are provenance-only. (4) Companion test evidence: the pre-fix test cases had to supply us:statutes/26/3102/a#input.employer_is_employer_of_taxpayer and three sibling cross-module inputs to make the gate pass; the fix deletes them, which is direct evidence the removed conjunct was load-bearing at runtime rather than dead code. (5) Provision verified at corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, provision sha256 52bb756b631434753de6fc041ed2769b52335607d5d30a7004e05839fbb93170; selection_basis was "no_toolchain_corpus_pin", so the release is a fallback rather than the fix-time pin, but 3505 has not been amended in a way that bears on this reading.
